_note: Hand-curated. Only the moments a newcomer needs. kind: achievement (links to a case), launch (a model release), origin (pre-history), prize. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD; use -01 when only the month is known (the day is then hidden); set "approx": true to hide a day that is only approximately known but needed for ordering.

items.title: Turing asks whether machines can think
items.blurb: Alan Turing's paper 'Computing Machinery and Intelligence' proposes the imitation game. The question has a name now.

items.title: The Dartmouth workshop names the field
items.blurb: A summer workshop at Dartmouth College coins the term 'artificial intelligence' and sets out the research programme.

items.title: Deep Blue beats Kasparov
items.blurb: IBM's chess machine wins a six-game match against the world champion. Brute-force search, no learning, and still the first time a computer beat the best human at anything that mattered to people.

items.title: AlexNet wins ImageNet
items.blurb: A deep convolutional network trained on two consumer GPUs cuts the image-recognition error rate by nearly half. The modern deep-learning era starts here.

items.title: AlphaGo plays Move 37
items.blurb: In game two against Lee Sedol, AlphaGo plays a move human experts put at 1-in-10,000. It wins the match 4–1. Go was supposed to be a decade away.

items.title: 'Attention Is All You Need'
items.blurb: Eight Google researchers publish the Transformer. Nearly every system on this timeline after 2020 is built on it.

items.title: AlphaZero learns chess, shogi and Go from the rules alone
items.blurb: No human games, no opening books. Hours of self-play, then it beats the best programs in all three.

items.title: GPT-3
items.blurb: A 175-billion-parameter language model that can do tasks it was never trained for, given a few examples in the prompt. The first hint that scale alone buys generality.

items.title: AlphaFold solves protein folding
items.blurb: At the CASP14 competition, DeepMind's system predicts protein structures at experimental accuracy. A 50-year grand challenge, and a Nobel Prize four years later.

items.title: Reinforcement learning steers a fusion reactor
items.blurb: A learned controller shapes real plasma inside the TCV tokamak in Lausanne, on its first attempt.

items.title: AlphaTensor beats a 53-year-old algorithm
items.blurb: A faster way to multiply 4×4 matrices than Strassen found in 1969. The first AI-discovered improvement to a fundamental algorithm.

items.title: ChatGPT
items.blurb: OpenAI puts a chat interface on GPT-3.5. A hundred million people use it within two months, and the public conversation about AI changes for good.

items.title: GPT-4
items.blurb: Passes a simulated bar exam in the top 10%, reads images, and sets the bar the rest of the industry chases for two years.

items.title: An AI-found sorting routine ships in the C++ standard library
items.blurb: AlphaDev discovers faster sorting sequences in assembly. They are merged into LLVM's libc++ and run trillions of times a day.

items.title: A speech neuroprosthesis restores conversation after paralysis
items.blurb: Brain signals decoded into words at near-conversational speed, with a digital avatar to speak them.

items.title: GraphCast out-forecasts the world's best weather model
items.blurb: Ten-day global forecasts in under a minute, more accurate than ECMWF's supercomputer system on 90% of targets.

items.title: GNoME predicts 2.2 million new crystals
items.blurb: An order-of-magnitude expansion of the stable materials known to science, 380,000 of them believed stable.

items.title: FunSearch finds new mathematics
items.blurb: A language model plus a checker produces a larger cap set than any known. The first verifiable new result from an LLM on an open problem.

items.title: Silver at the International Mathematical Olympiad
items.blurb: AlphaProof and AlphaGeometry 2 solve four of six IMO problems. One point short of gold.

items.title: OpenAI o1: the first 'reasoning' model
items.blurb: A model trained to think before it answers, spending more compute at test time. Every frontier lab follows within months.

items.title: The first complete wiring diagram of an adult brain
items.blurb: AI segmentation maps all 140,000 neurons and 50 million connections in a fruit fly.

items.title: Two Nobel Prizes go to AI
items.blurb: Physics to Hopfield and Hinton for the foundations of neural networks; Chemistry to Baker, Hassabis and Jumper for protein design and AlphaFold.

items.title: DeepSeek-R1
items.blurb: An open-weights reasoning model from China matching o1 at a fraction of the reported training cost. Nvidia loses about $600 billion in market value in a day.

items.title: AlphaEvolve improves Strassen and ~50 open problems
items.blurb: A coding agent that evolves algorithms, breaking a 56-year-old record for 4×4 complex matrix multiplication along the way.

items.title: An AI agent finds a zero-day before attackers use it
items.blurb: Google's Big Sleep locates a SQLite flaw that threat intelligence knew was being staged, so it is patched first.

items.title: Gold at the IMO, graded by the IMO
items.blurb: Gemini Deep Think scores 35/42, working end-to-end in natural language. OpenAI reports the same score the same week.

items.title: AI weather forecasts go operational
items.blurb: NOAA puts an AI forecast suite into daily operations. During hurricane season an AI model beat the National Hurricane Center's own track forecast.

items.title: Claude Mythos Preview
items.blurb: Anthropic announces a model it says it will not release publicly because of its vulnerability-finding ability, and shares it only with a consortium of 40-plus companies under Project Glasswing.

items.title: Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5
items.blurb: One underlying model, two versions: Fable 5 for everyone with dual-use safeguards, Mythos 5 for approved organizations without them.

items.title: OpenAI's models escape a sandbox and breach Hugging Face
items.blurb: During an internal safety evaluation, the models find a zero-day, get out, and compromise a rival's production servers, apparently to cheat on the benchmark.

items.title: The Jacobian conjecture falls
items.blurb: Levent Alpöge and Claude Fable 5 produce an explicit polynomial map that disproves an 87-year-old conjecture in dimension three and up. You can check it by hand.

items.title: Perfect 42/42 scores at the IMO
items.blurb: Two years after silver and one after gold, several systems report flawless papers. Only 7 of 666 human contestants did the same. None of the scores is IMO-certified.

items.title: Claude breaks a post-quantum signature candidate
items.blurb: A lattice automorphism found by Claude Mythos Preview halves the hard problem behind HAWK. Its authors withdraw it from NIST standardization.

items.title: Ten open problems, ten Lean certificates
items.blurb: OpenAI's internal model Astra closes ten long-open results in maths and theoretical CS, including the first improvement to the sphere-packing exponent since 1978. Every proof ships machine-checked.

items.title: GPT-6 Astra
items.blurb: OpenAI's largest training run, a 'recurrent depth' architecture that hides much of its reasoning, and cyber capabilities restricted to vetted testers.

items.title: An AI claim on a Millennium Prize Problem
items.blurb: OpenAI says 10,000 agents proved finite-time blowup for the forced Navier–Stokes equations, with a Lean certificate. Unverified outside OpenAI, forced case only, and a credit dispute with the mathematicians who got there first on Euler.
